For new valves, use the manufacturer's standard packings if they meet the guidelines discussed in "Packing Guidelines from Valve Manufacturers" on page 1400-41.
The best performing flexible graphite (die-formed rings) valve packings for hydrocarbon service are:
  ◆ Garlock EVSP  ◆ Simplified Garlock 70#
The best performing flexible graphite packing for field installation is Garlock 1395FEP, Slade 3000G and RM Graphaseal have had mixed results.
The best performing non-graphite packings are DuPont Kalrez and Garlock Teflon.
Before using any packing, check the compatibility of the packing material with the intended service.

All existing packing should be removed carefully, preferably with a water jet, before installing new packing.
Visually inspect the valve condition to make sure that no obvious flaws, such as a corroded stem, exist. A damaged valve may need to be reconditioned or replaced (repacking alone may not be sufficient).
Manufacturer instructions, if available, should be followed when installing packing.
While packing, each ring should be compressed 2-3%. When the entire packing set is in place, it should be compressed to about 20-25% less than the original height (30% for braided graphite systems). Alternatively, a torque wrench could be used, if available, to tighten the packing gland to the manufacturer's specifications.

The first attempt at repair should be to tighten the packing gland and fittings. A torque wrench can be used if a bolt torque is specified.
If the valve can be taken out of service, it should be checked for corrosion damage and repacked using low emission valve packing.
If the valve cannot be taken out of service, and it cannot wait until the next shutdown for repair (because the material is toxic or a compliance violation would result), the valve can be leak sealed.
Injection of soft packing can be successful in stopping leaks but should only be used if no other options are available.
There are many factors such as needing staging or a fresh air supply that should be taken into consideration when deciding whether to attempt an immediate repair or to place the valve on the "allowable leaker" list.
